name: SKM Egg Products Export (India) Ltd
title: SKM Egg Products Export (India) Ltd - 532143 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: SKM Egg Products FY26 sales rose 58% to ₹767 crore and PAT crossed ₹100 crore for the first time (₹102 crore).
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 results: sales up 58% YoY to ₹767 crore, operating profit about ₹163 crore, PBT ₹136 crore and PAT ₹102 crore, the first year above ₹100 crore PAT. Q4 FY26 sales were ₹197 crore, with PBT ₹41 crore and PAT ₹32 crore against ₹9.7 crore and ₹6.22 crore a year earlier. Management said powder capacity is now running at full utilisation, so FY27 volume growth will be modest. The company is funding a ₹400 crore layer-shed expansion (about 20 lakh birds, completion targeted 2028-29) and is bringing the associate SKM Universal into the listed entity.

segments.name: Egg powder (export)
segments.commentary: About 7,000 tonnes of powder today with a stated target of 10,000 tonnes over roughly five years; powder capacity was 7,320 tonnes as of 2023. Management said FY27 powder volume growth will be small because capacity is fully used.

segments.name: Shellac (export and domestic)
segments.commentary: Export business is about ₹100 crore and domestic about ₹40 crore; management expects this to keep growing and to be a source of FY27 growth.

segments.name: Branded / value-added egg products
segments.commentary: Products include egg in tetra-pack, egg liquid, egg white cube and Egg Pro protein drink. Management reformulated Egg Pro for launch in June, and an R&D division is planned within six months. Revenue from these products has been small so far.

guidance_outlook: Management said the ₹1,000 crore revenue target is for 2030, not FY27.
FY27 powder top-line growth will be modest because the company is at full capacity; shellac and domestic growth expected to add to it.
Q1 FY27 realisation expected to continue near the Q4 level (~₹722/kg powder terms), with some international market changes but no major impact expected.
The ₹400 crore layer-shed capex is a cost-saving, bottom-line investment (not a top-line one) and is expected to be completed by FY28-29, taking the flock from about 20 lakh to 40 lakh birds.
Management said it expects about ₹0.20 per egg of production-cost savings from the new system, and a gross margin of about ₹0.50 per egg.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 sales volumes and realisation per kg, and what is the outlook for FY27–28, including the ₹1,000 crore target and the SKM Universal consideration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no exact volume or consideration figures on the call. It said capacity is full, realisation rose through FY26 with a Q4 dip on mix (~₹722/kg powder), and the ₹1,000 crore goal is for 2030. For SKM Universal, the valuation is about ₹37 crore for the whole company; the group already holds 26%, so the 74% stake costs about ₹27.75 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the country-wise revenue split and competitive position, and what is driving elevated egg prices in Japan?
qa_highlights.answer: The country split was declined as it is not public. Competitors are European producers in Japan and Russia. Management said it earns about 5% more than competitors. Price strength was attributed to bird flu culls, which take about two years to repopulate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current capacity, the 400 crore capex timeline, and the value-added product plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Flock is moving toward 40 lakh birds by 2028-29. The capex is a cost-saving investment, not a revenue driver. Management is developing value-added products (Egg Pro relaunch, egg white cube) and an R&D unit. Shellac export and domestic are also growing.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Indian producers not consistently profitable outside bird flu cycles, and how are contracts priced and hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bird-flu disruptions are sporadic and under control, with vaccination under discussion with the government. Contracts are mostly 3–6 months, priced on cost and competition, and the forex hedge is currently only about 30%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected ROC on the new EC-shed project and what drives FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exact ROC figures would follow later. It said the project cuts production cost by about ₹0.20 per egg. FY27 growth is expected to be small in powder and larger in shellac and domestic sales.

qa_highlights.question: How does the USD–EUR rate affect other expenses, and will the investor presentation be shared?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe is a small share of business and most pricing is in USD. Russia is invoiced in rupees and rubles, and Japan from H2. The presentation will be uploaded to the website.

risks_watch: Bird flu outbreaks drive the price cycle in both directions; India's current situation is described as sporadic, but a major outbreak would affect supply and realisation.

Power outages were noted during the call, and the new capex is roughly 2.5 times the company's FY26 PAT. Funding relies on a ₹302 crore bank loan, and the ₹403 crore cost may change with foreign-currency payments.
Only about 30% of forex exposure is hedged at present, against a normal 60–70%.
Management gave no numbers on capex ROC, FY27 volume or the SKM Universal consideration, and said exact numbers would follow by email, so disclosure on these is still open.
Value-added and branded products are early-stage, with an R&D division due in six months and the Egg Pro relaunch in June.
Management said it cannot share country-wise revenue, so the market concentration risk (Japan, Russia, Europe) cannot be assessed.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the FY26 numbers and capacity growth but cautious and sometimes evasive on forward numbers, declining country splits, ROC, FY27 volumes and the SKM Universal consideration, and deferring detail to email follow-up.
key_quotes: And the profit after tax first time in the lifetime history crossing 100 crores profit after tax.
Capex of 400 crores is this is not a top line growth investment. It is a bottom line.
Because egg is the cheapest protein that is available.
capex_capacity: Current flock about 20 lakh layer birds per the MD (5 lakh owned earlier plus leased and phase-one EC sheds); target about 40 lakh birds by 2028-29 with the ongoing EC shed phase 2 adding 20 lakh birds

Layer-shed capex of ₹400 crore (cost cited as ₹403 crore, may vary because a substantial part of payments is in foreign currency); funding is own funds plus a ₹101 crore bank term loan and ₹302 crore bank loan; management said net cost of funds is about 4.5% after a 3% interest subsidy

Management described the capex as a bottom-line, cost-saving investment: about ₹0.20 per egg production-cost saving versus conventional open sheds, and a gross margin of at least ₹0.50 per egg; it would remove procurement of about 4–5 lakh eggs per day from market
Powder capacity 7,320 tonnes (as of 2023); company said it is operating at full capacity and does not foresee a big capacity increase in FY27
Powder expansion plan to about 10,000 tonnes; management said the capex analysis would be ready by end of next quarter or after, and reaching 7,000–10,000 tonnes could take about five years

Breaking capacity history cited on call: 22 lakh eggs per day after the 2020s expansion; biogas plant with 70-ton digesters generating power from litter; a 1 lakh-bird layer shed completed in first phase
Management did not give ROC on the new EC-shed project; said exact numbers would be provided later
Japan branch targeted to be established around July-end 2026 per the call; Japan share cited at about 10% of total imports
demand_pricing: FY26 export volume 7,126 metric tonnes (all-time high); management did not give FY26 sales volume or FY27–28 volume numbers, and said FY27 powder growth will be small because capacity is full, with growth coming from shellac and domestic

Average powder-terms realisation about ₹722/kg in Q4 FY26; realisation rose Q1 to Q3 and dipped in Q4 on product mix; management expects Q1 FY27 to continue near this level despite some international market changes
Shellac: export about ₹100 crore and domestic about ₹40 crore; management expects continued growth

Competition: European producers in Japan and Russia, US present in Russia; elsewhere mainly Indian players; management claimed about 5% higher realisation than competitors, attributed to quality and reputation
Pricing: about 70–75% of business on contracts of typically 3 or 6 months; balance spot; prices set on cost and competitor pricing, not benchmarked to any index
Forex: normally 60–70% of exposure hedged with one-year forwards; currently only about 30% covered due to volatility; Russia invoiced in rupees and rubles, Japan from H2 FY27, Europe offered in euro

Demand drivers: bird flu culls reduce supply and lift prices, with about two years to repopulate; India benefited as an alternate supply source; management said egg is the cheapest protein and domestic egg consumption is rising

Branded/value-added: Egg Pro drink reformulated for June launch, egg white cube shelf life being extended, R&D division planned in about six months; management said value-added export is hard, so the initial focus is India
₹1,000 crore revenue target is for 2030, not FY27; management said it is gearing up in powder and egg capacity for this

SKM Universal acquisition: valuation about ₹37 crore for the whole company; company holds 26%, the 74% stake implies about ₹27.75 crore outflow; rationale includes windmill division savings and bringing the brand into the listed entity

adds.what: Layer-shed expansion (EC sheds) adding ~20 lakh layer birds, taking flock from ~20 lakh to ~40 lakh
Powder capacity expansion to ~10,000 tonnes from 7,320 tonnes; capex analysis not yet ready, reaching 7,000-10,000 t could take ~5 years

growth.why: FY27 powder volume growth guided only as 'small' because the 7,320 t plant is at full utilisation; the ₹1,000 cr target is for 2030, the ₹400 cr layer-shed is a bottom-line cost project live in ~2028-29, and Q4 revenue grew ~9% (₹197 cr vs ₹180 cr) with PAT up sharply on a low base.
